## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Fix "Restore False for requirements with no criteria" before merging: `requirement_proven` now reports an empty requirement as proven, which reverses a release-review decision even though the PR says no behavior change is intended. Every other changed line matched the mechanical typing, logging and `itemgetter` rewrite, checked by pattern counts across the full diff.

## Changes
The PR replaces `typing.List`/`Dict` with built-in generics and `log.warn` with `log.warning` across 180 record handlers. It also switches `by_name` to `operator.itemgetter`, rewrites `requirement_proven` to compare a `sum` with `len`, and adds a root-level `review.txt`.

## Critical
- app/handlers/h091_requirements.py:13 — correctness — Restore False for requirements with no criteria — `requirement_proven([])` now returns `True`, because `sum(...) == len(criteria)` evaluates `0 == 0`; the removed `bool(criteria) and all(...)` returned `False`. Line 10 still logs "requirement has no criteria" and then falls through to this check. — A requirement with no criteria now passes release review as proven, though the PR says no behavior change is intended. — Fix: Return `bool(criteria) and all(item["proven"] for item in criteria)` again, or return `False` inside the `if not criteria:` branch, and extend `tests/test_handlers.py::test_requirement_proof` with the empty-list case.
